negligently by non-applicant no. 2, causing injuries to the deceased.
On the next day deceased was taken to District Hospital Sidhi where
after primary treatment referred to SGMH Rewa where he died
during treatment on 7/10/2023. Thereafter marg was registered and
after investigation challan ‘was filed. Applicants claimed
compensation jointly and severally against the non-applicants.

(शा) Grounds of appeal

well as of facts by holding the Appellant-insurance company liable to

making appellant liable to the pay compensation are totally perverse,
illegal and bad and therefore, deserves to be set aside.
(B) For that, Tribunal below has not rightly appreciated the objections
raised by appellant and documents produced on record.
(C) For that, the impugned award is contrary to the facts and law
available on record. हु
(D) For that, the FIR of the alleged accident is lodged against the alleged
vehicle after 80 days of the accident i.e. for the accident dated
18/09/2023, the FIR was lodged on 7/12/2023 falsely involving the

--- PAGE 11 ---
(3)
alleged vehicle just to realize compensation money from the
insurance company of the vehicle.
(E) एक that, as per paragraph no. 9 of the award, deceased died during
treatment on 7/10/2023; between this period from 18/09/2023 till
7/10/2023, the involvement of the alleged vehicle was not revealed.
Thereafter for about 80 days after the accident till the lodging of FIR
on 7/12/2023 the involvement of the alleged vehicle is not revealed.
From the entire evidence produced before Tribunal and police
challan, it is not becoming clear as to how the involvement of the
motorcycle no. MP-66-ZA-4044 was revealed in the accident.
| Applicants have not produced any reliable eye witness to prove the
involvement of vehicle no. MP-66-ZA-4044 in the accident. The
burden lies upon the claimants to prove their case and proof of rash
and negligent driving by the driver of alleged vehicle is sine qua non,
that burden has not been discharged by the claimants. Accident and
rash and negligent driving of the driver is not proved by the
applicants before Tribunal but the learned Tribunal has grossly erred
in holding the accident proved and saddling joint and several liability
against the non-applicants.
(F) For that, alleged offending vehicle is a motorcycle and non-applicant
no. 1 — Vishal Singh is owner and non-applicant no. 2 — Sandeep
Dubey is driver of the alleged motorcycle. Here it is noteworthy to
mention that one is resident of*Sidhi and other is resident of Rewa;
there is no relation between these 2 persons, they are not related to
each other, alleged motorcycle is a two-wheeler. These facts coupled
with the fact that alleged offending vehicle was involved in the

accident after about 80 days of the accident, clearly entails that
alleged vehicle has falsely begn involved in the accident just to
realize compensation money from the insurance company of this
vehicle. More so, how the registration number of the offending
vehicle has come on record is not clear from the documents of entire

(G) For that, deceased was a bachelor and his father is also one of the
applicant aged about 48 yrs., in such circumstances it is not proved
that applicant no. 3 and 4 who are siblings of the deceased are in any
: way dependent upon the deceased. Tribunal has grossly erred in
taking dependency as 2/3. Under the circumstances of the case proper
dependency is % and not 2/3. Thus on this count compensation
calculated deserves to be reduced.
(H) For that, Tribunal has erred in law in awarding loss of consortium to
brother and sisters. Consortium can be either spousal or filial or
ह parental but the Tribunal has erred in awarding consortium to brother
and sisters of the deceased, which is liable to be reduced.
(1) For that, Tribunal again erred in awarding rate of interest as 9%
which is at higher side and unreasonable. Looking to the prevailing
rate of interest upon the FDs, interest rate cannot be more than 6%.

// AWARD //
(Pronounced today on 16" September, 2025)
Claimants have filed this petition u/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles
Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act") for recovery of
damages to the tune of हैं 64,36,000/- (Rupees sixty four lakh thirty six
thousand only) under different heads for death of Late Anjani Singh
caused due to vehicular accident.
2. It is not in dispute that the offending vehicle motorcycle
bearing registration no. MP 66 ZA 4044 is of the ownership of
respondent number 1 and was insured with respondent number 3
(Insurance Company) on 18-09-2023 under comprehensive policy.
3. The necessary facts to adjudicate present claim petition
as culled out from the claim petition in brief are that claimants are
parents (mother & father) and younger sister and brother of deceased.
On 18-09-2023, deceased Anjani Singh went towards his village on
foot. At around 04:30 pm, when he reached near house of Ramgopal
Singh, suddenly driver of offending vehicle Honda motorcycle bearing
registration no. MP 66 ZA 4044 driving in rash and negligent manner
--- PAGE 17 ---
©
3 MACC No. 1084/2023
Parvati Singh & ors v. Vishal Singh Gond & ors.
came from rear side and hit him. Due to the collision, deceased fell
down and sustained severe injuries in his head and chest. On the next
day, deceased was taken to District Hospital Sidhi, where after primary
treatment he was referred to SGMH Rewa, where during the treatment,
he died on 07-10-2023. His post mortem was conducted. On the basis
of intimation, zero Marg was registered at SGMH Police outpost,
Rewa. Marg was transferred to the PS Majhauli, District Sidhi. On the
basis of Marg inquiry, FIR of Crime No. 1340/2023 was registered at
PS Majhauli, District Sidhi. After the investigation, chargesheet was
wo filed before the jurisdictional JMFC for trial.
जा
4. It is further stated by claimants that before the accident
deceased Anjani Singh was about 22 years old and was unmarried. He
was an skilled labour and was working as artisan and was earning हैं
700/- per day i.e. हैं 21,000/- (Rupees twenty one thousand per month).
Claimants were dependent upon him and it was certain that the income
of deceased would increase in the future. Due to the untimely death of
deceased, claimants have suffered loss of dependency and other losses.
The said accident was caused by R-2 by driving the offending vehicle
of R-1 in rash and negligent manner and was under the insurance
agreement of R-3. Therefore, they are entitled to damages of %
64,36,000/- (Rupees sixty four lakh thirty six thousand only) from all
the respondents jointly and severally along with interest at market rate.
Hence, this petition.
5. Respondent number 1 and 2 have not appeared despite
service of summons, therefore, they have been proceeded ex-parte.
6. In response to the claim petition, insurance company R-3
has filed its written statement and stated that no such accident took
place as is claimed in their petition by claimants. Deceased himself
--- PAGE 18 ---
4 MACC No. 1084/2023
Parvati Singh & ors v. Vishal Singh Gond & ors.
was negligent and is responsible for the accident. It is further stated
that FIR was registered belatedly after about twenty days. Respondent
no. 1 and 2 in collusion with the claim petitioners has implanted the
offending vehicle in order to receive compensation. The offending
vehicle was driven in breach of the terms of insurance policy. There is
no valid driving licence of driver R-2. Therefore, insurance company is
not responsible to pay any damages. Further, due to non-compliance
section 134(C), 147, 150, 158(6) and 170 of the Act insurance Ge
company be absolved from any liability. There is no proof of income aA
of deceased. The amount of damages claimed by the petitioners is जन
highly exaggerated and imaginary. Interest cannot be allowed on
award. On these grounds, it is prayed that the claim petition be
dismissed.
7. From the pleadings of the parties, following issues were
framed. Findings on each issue is given against it and reasons
thereafter:-
ISSUE FINDING

REASONS AND FINDINGS
Issue No. 1 .-
8. It is the settled proposition of law that an action under
section 166 of the Act is founded on the principle of fault liability, the
proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine
--- PAGE 20 ---
(2)
6 MACC No. 1084/2023
Parvati Singh & ors v. Vishal Singh Gond & ors.
qua non. However, the standard of proof is not as strict as is applied in
criminal cases and evidence is to be tested only on the touchstone of
preponderance of probabilities. Holistic view is to be taken while
dealing with the claim petition based upon negligence. Strict rules of
evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims
Tribunal. Reference may be made to the judgments of Hon'ble Apex
Court in Bimla Devi & Others v. Himachal Road Transport
Corporation & Others, (2009) 13 SC 530, Parmeshwari v. we
Amirchand & Others, 2011 (1) SCR 1096 and Mangla Ram v. 1,
Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. & Others, 2018 LawSuit (SC) & %
303. Noval
9. Claimant Vishnudev Singh (PW-1) has stated that his
son Anjani Singh died in road accident which occurred on 18-09-2023
at around 04:30 pm in village Ama Kholi Bakwa Gijwar by a
motorcycle. He has stated that on the date of incident his son Anjani
Singh Gond went to neighbor's home on foot. When he reached about
500 meter away from his house, suddenly a motorcycle bearing
registration no. MP 66 ZA 4044 came from rear side rashly and
negligently and dashed him, which caused serious injuries to deceased
and during the treatment he died on 07-10-2023.
10. There is nothing material elicited from the cross-
examination of the claimant Vishnudev Singh (PW-1), which would
impeach his credibility or trustworthiness. Respondents could not
impeach his testimony through litmus test of cross-examination and he
is found to have successfully withstood the cross-examination.
11. Claimant has filed certified copies of final report in FIR
no. 1340/2023 registered at PS Majhauli, District Sidhi with regard to
the accident in question (Ex.P.-1 to Ex.P.-14). Furthermore, claimant
--- PAGE 21 ---
(08)
7 MACC No. 1084/2023
ह Parvati Singh & ors v. Vishal Singh Gond & ors.
has also placed reliance on the chargesheet/final report under section
173 CrPC filed by IO (Ex.P.-1), FIR (Ex.P.-2), Marg intimation (Ex.P.-
3), intimation given by SGMH, Rewa to police outpost (Ex.P.-4),
notice u/s 175 Cr.P.C. (Ex.P.-5), Naksha Panchayatnama (Ex.P-6),

issued by District Hospital, Sidhi (Ex.P-8 and Ex.P-9), patients intake

i postmortem report (Ex.P-11), site plan (Ex.P-12), seizure memo of
Je offending vehicle alongwith documents (Ex.P-13) and notice ws
< > 41(A) Cr.P.C. (Ex.P-14) on the basis of which R-2 namely Sandeep
ae - Kumar Dubey (accused in State case) has been charged for offences
punishable u/s 304A IPC by the investigating agency after arriving at
“+ the conclusion on the basis of investigation carried out by it that the
accident in question had occurred due to rashness and negligence on
the part of R-2 (driver of offending vehicle).
12. A bare perusal of certified copy of postmortem report
(Ex.P.-11) of the deceased Anjani Singh reveals that the opinion as
cause of death is given as “Death is due to cardio respiratory
failure as a result of head injury and its complications.” There is
clear mention of history of RTA (road traffic accident) and multiple
injuries sustained in RTA in post mortem report. Deceased had healed
wound in form of hypo pigmented scar present on right leg mid 1/3
part anterio medial aspect of size 7cm X 4cm. In Naksha
Panchayatnama (Ex.P-6), cause of death is opined by all the panchas
to be road accident. Said documents have not been disputed and thus
corroborates the ocular testimony of Vishnudev Singh (PW-1) as
discussed above. Therefore, death of Anjani Singh in vehicular
accident stands to be proved.
--- PAGE 22 ---
(9)
(9)
8 MACC No. 1084/2023
Parvati Singh & ors v. Vishal Singh Gond & ors.
13. FIR (Ex.P.-2) would show that accident occurred on 18-
09-2023 and FIR was lodged on 07-12-2023 after nearly 80 days of
the accident. But treatment related documents issued by District
Hospital Sidhi (Ex.P-8 & Ex.P-9) and patients intake and output chart
(Ex.P-10) clearly shows that due to accident deceased was admitted at
District Hospital Sidhi on 19-09-2023 and after primary treatment, he
was referred to SGMH Rewa for further treatment. Marg intimation
(Ex.P-3) and MLC death intimation (Ex.P.-4) clearly shows that after (4
referral from District Hospital Sidhi deceased was admitted at SGMH ,
Rewa on 19-09-2023 and during treatment he died on 07-10-2023 at A =
around 10:43 am. Intimation in this regard was given by Dr. Deepa 5
Singh to Police Chauki SGMH Rewa on 07-10-2023. After intimation
delay in lodging the FIR is the part of hospital and police, and not in
the part of claimant.
14. There is clear cut mention of RTA in treatment related
documents issued by District Hospital Sidhi (Ex.P-8 & Ex.P-9). It was
therefore, duty of the treating hospital to inform police to take action.
There is no reason for the claimants to rush to police instead of taking
care of the deceased. Death intimation given by duty doctor to police
Chauki SGMH Rewa (Ex.P-4), Naksha Panchayatnama (Ex.P-6) as
well as application for postmortem and postmortem report (Ex.P-11),
have clear cut mention of RTA. Therefore, the intimation of RTA was
promptly given by the claimants and if there is any delay, it is
attributable to the hospital administration or police for which claimant
cannot be held responsible.
15. Seizure memo of offending vehicle (Ex.P.-13) reveals
that offending vehicle was seized from the possession of Sandeep
Kumar Dubey R-2 and he has also submitted the registration
--- PAGE 23 ---
9 MACC No. 1084/2023
Parvati Singh & ors v. Vishal Singh Gond & ors.
certificate and other documents. Therefore, the factum of accident is
established and there is no possibility of false implication of
respondent no.1 & 2 and/or false involvement of aforesaid offending
vehicle at the instance of claimant herein.
16. In National Insurance Co. v. Pushpa Rana 2009 ACJ
287 Delhi, Hon'ble Delhi High Court has laid down that completion of
है! investigation and filing of chargesheet under relevant sections are
कै sufficient proof of negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
2 4) Further, Hon'ble Supreme Court in Ranjeet and Another v. Abdul
“%? Kayam Neb and Another (Arising out of SLP (C) No.10351 of
~ 2019 decided on 25.02.2025), has discussed the aforesaid issues and
held that — “4. It is settled in law that once a charge sheet has been
filed and the driver has been held negligent, no further evidence is
required to prove that the bus was being negligently driven by the bus
driver. Even if the eyewitnesses are not examined, that will not be
fatal to prove the death of the deceased due to negligence of the bus
driver."
17. Moreover, apart from the claimant, R-2, driver of the
offending vehicle, was the other material witness who could have
thrown sufficient light as to how and under what circumstances, the
accident in question took place. However, he did not enter into witness
box during the course of inquiry. Thus, an adverse inference is liable
to be drawn against him for not entering into the witness box, to the
effect that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of
offending vehicle by him. Reliance may be placed on Division Bench
judgment of Hon'ble Madhya Pradesh High Court in Chanda Devi v.
Rajendra Singh, 2004 ACJ 63.
--- PAGE 24 ---
6)
®
10 MACC No. 1084/2023
Parvati Singh & ors v. Vishal Singh Gond & ors.
18. R-3 insurance company has pleaded contributory
negligence on part of deceased Anjani Singh on the ground that
deceased not moving carefully and suddenly came in front of
offending vehicle due to which accident was occurred. But in this
regard, no evidence is adduced by the respondent which could show
decease's negligence in any manner. So, I am not impressed with this
argument. It was the duty of driver of offending vehicle to take
precaution. Hence, there is no contributory negligence in this case. & a
19. Thus, in view of the aforesaid discussion and the eR
evidence on record, it is held that the claimant has been successfully
able to prove on the basis of preponderance of probabilities that
deceased Anjani Singh died in road accident which took place on 18-
09-2023 at around 04:30 pm in village Ama Kholi Bakwa Gijwar, Post
Tikri, District Sidhi due to rash and negligent driving on the part of R-
2, driver of offending vehicle motorcycle bearing registration number
MP 66 ZA 4044. Accordingly, finding of Tribunal on issue no. 1
stands to be proved.
Issue No. 2 .-
20. Claimants has filed a photocopy of insurance policy no. :
MR505093 having validity of liability section from 30-10-2022 to 29-
10-2027 in which engine number and chassis number are mentioned
and match with the same as mentioned in seizure memo (Ex.P-13). R-
3 insurance company has not denied the said insurance policy. A bare
perusal of the policy reveals that it is package policy on the date of
accident i.e. 18-09-2023. Accordingly, finding of Tribunal on issue
no.2 stands to be proved.

11 MACC No. 1084/2023
Parvati Singh & ors v. Vishal Singh Gond & ors.
Issue No. 3.-
21. Burden to prove breach lies upon the insurance
company. Insurance company R-3 has contended that there is breach
of policy on the ground of lack of valid driving licence. Seizure memo
(Ex.P.-13) shows that driving licence bearing no.MP1720130182202
D3 of R-2 Sandeep Kumar Dubey was seized after the accident on 08-12-
BD 2023, validity of which mentioned as 24-07-2033. Print out of details
a oy of said driving licence is also on record which reveals that it was valid
wa ९५८ for driving non-transport vehicle from 25-07-2013 to 24-07-2033.
Therefore, breach of policy as claimed by R-3 insurance company is
not established and finding of Tribunal on issue no. 3 is recorded as
‘not proved.’
Issue No. 4 .-
22. In view of the finding on issue no. 1, 2 and 3, claimant is
entitled to get damages/compensation, however, the quantum of
compensation still needs to be adjudicated. Section 168 of the Act
enjoins upon the Claims Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to
make an award determining the amount of compensation, which
appears to be just and reasonable. As per settled law, compensation is
not expected to be windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.
23. Certain principles for delineating just compensation in
death cases were laid down by Hon’ble Supreme Court in Sarla
Verma and Others v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr. (2009) 6
SCC 121. Further, the guidelines have been reiterated and modified by
the Constitution Bench of Hon’ble Supreme Court in National
Insurance Company v. Pranay Sethi & Ors., 2017 ACJ 2700,
decided on 31.10.2017, laying down the general principles for
ह computation of compensation in death cases.
--- PAGE 26 ---
. (58)
(52
12 MACC No. 1084/2023
Parvati Singh & ors v. Vishal Singh Gond & ors.
24. In the facts of present case, the compensation would be
assessed on the basis of evidence adduced on record by the claimants.
lL Loss of dependency :
(1) Age of deceased
25. Claimant Vishnudev Singh (PW-1) is father of deceased
who has deposed that deceased Anjani Singh was 22 years old at the है
time of death. Certified copy of post mortem report (Ex.P.-11) >
describes his age as 22 years. In the claim petition his age was
mentioned to be 22 years. Though no other document to prove age of
deceased is filed on record, there is no reason to doubt the age of
deceased as mentioned in post mortem in the absence of any other
material. Therefore, age of deceased Anjani Singh is assessed to be 22
years at the time of accident.
(2) Assessment of income of deceased
26. Claimant Vishnudev Singh (PW-1) has deposed that his
son Anjani Singh was an artisan (कारीगर) and he was earning हैं 700/-
per day. However, no document is filed on record to prove his
vocation. What kind of artistry he was involved in has not been stated.
27. A-young man of 22 years age can not be assumed to be a
skilled artisan. Artistry requires skill which can only be earned by
experience. But claimants have not filed any documents which shows
the experience of deceased Anjani Singh, by which he can be assumed
to be a skilled artist. Therefore, in the absence of any specific proof,
deceased can only be assumed to be an unskilled labour. As an
unskilled labour, his income is assessed as हैं 9,650/- (Rupees nine
thousand six hundred fifty only) per month under the notification
--- PAGE 27 ---
13 MACC No. 1084/2023
Parvati Singh & ors v. Vishal Singh Gond & ors.
issued under Minimum Wages Act on the date of accident i.e., on 18-
09-2023.
(3) Calculation of future prospects ह
28. Deceased Anjani Singh was not in any permanent
DB: employment. Thus assuming as a self employed/fixed salary person of
¥ a 22 years old, as per directions in Pranay Sethi (supra), 40% addition
» Ay under future prospects is awarded. Accordingly, future prospects of the
ay deceased are assessed as 40% of the notional income i.e. हैं 9,650/- x
, 40% which stands at हैं 3,860/- per month.
(4) Deduction towards personal living expenses
29. Admittedly, deceased was unmarried man with four
dependents (two parents, one younger brother and an younger sister)
at the time of death, hence, as per Pranay Sethi (supra), 1/3 of the
income is be deducted towards personal expenses.
(5) Selection of multiplier :
30. In Pranay Sethi (supra), multiplier is prescribed for 21-
25 years as 18. Hence, the multiplier of 18 would be applicable in the
case in hand.
(6) Costs of medical treatment :
"31. Claimant have not claimed any amount in regard of
decease's treatment and also not filed any document regarding
expenses. However, deceased was taken to SGMH, Rewa and died on
07-10-2023 after 20 days of accident. He remained under treatment
for nearly 20 days. Looking to the nature of injuries, even if no
expenses were incurred in Government Hospital, a lump sum amount
of हैं 30,000/- (Rupees thirty thousand only) may be awarded including
expenses for treatment, caretaker, attendant, special diet etc.
--- PAGE 28 ---
@
(2
14 MACC No. 1084/2023
Parvati Singh & ors v. Vishal Singh Gond & ors.
IL. Damages under Conventional Heads
32. In Pranay Sethi (supra), Hon'ble Supreme Court has
held that reasonable figures on conventional heads, namely, loss of
consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses should be added @ 7%
40,000/-, हैं 15,000/- and % 15,000/- respectively and the aforesaid
amounts should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years
from 31.10.2017. Since date of death is 07-10-2023, 10% increase in &
above conventional heads is to be awarded. Therefore, claimants are ‘
entitled to हैं 44,000/-, हैं 16,500/- and हैं 16,500/- respectively on A
account of loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses
respectively. Further, in view of Three Judge Bench judgment of
Hon’ble Supreme Court in United India Insurance Co. Ltd. v.
Satinder Kaur @ Satwinder Kaur & Ors., (2021) 11 SCC 780, loss
of consortium has to be fixed for each of the LRs who were living at
the time of his death. Since, deceased was survived by two parents and
one younger brother and one younger sister, therefore, the claimants
are entitled to a sum of % 2,09,000/- (44,000 x 4 + 16,500 + 16,500)
under this head.

Interest .-
35. Having regard to the prevailing rate of interest and the
judgments of Hon'ble Supreme Court including Erudhaya Priya vs
State Express Transport, 2020 ACJ 2159, interest @ 9% per annum
is suitable to be awarded on the total award amount from the date of
claim petition till actual realization of Award amount/compensation.
Claim petitioner was not responsible for delay in adducing evidence
--- PAGE 30 ---
@

16 MACC No. 1084/2023
Parvati Singh & ors v. Vishal Singh Gond & ors.
during inquiry. Insurance company has taken considerable time to file
written statement. Therefore, rate of interest on award amount is
awarded as 9% per annum.
Liability .-
36. In this case, as per material on record, R-2 was the driver & A
and the registered owner of the offending vehicle. Insurance company A
R-3 has failed to establish breach. Since there is no statutory defence, oR
therefore, the compensation is also payable by the insurance company
of offending vehicle. Hence, keeping in view the entirety of the facts
and circumstances involved in the present case, liability falls on the
shoulders of all the respondents jointly and severally. Therefore, R-1,
R-2 and R-3 are held to be liable to pay jointly and severely the
compensation and award amount in question to the claimants as held
above. Issue no. 4 is decided accordingly.
Issue No. 6 .-
37. R3 Insurance Company has contended that the claimants
are resident of district Sidhi and the accident also took place in their
own village. This Tribunal at Rewa has no territorial jurisdiction to
hear the petition and therefore, the petition is liable to be dismissed.
38. However, the array of the claim petition sufficiently
makes it clear that respondent number 2 Sandeep Dubey is resident of
village Gurh, district Rewa which falls under the jurisdiction of this
Tribunal. Section 166 of the Act provide that a claim petition may be
filed at the option of the claimant, either to the Claims Tribunal having
jurisdiction over the area in which the accident occurred or to the
Claims Tribunal within the local limits of whose jurisdiction the
claimant resides or carries on business or within the local limits of
whose jurisdiction the defendant resides. Since, one of the respondents
--- PAGE 31 ---
(28)
@
17 MACC No. 1084/2023
Parvati Singh & ors v. Vishal Singh Gond & ors.
recite within the territorial jurisdiction of this Tribunal, I have
jurisdiction to hear and decide the matter. Resultantly, the finding of
Tribunal on issue number 6 is "not proved.”
